despinStress.formula:
DESPIN MEMBRANE STRESS about paleo-spin axis w0. theta = colatitude FROM w0 = angle(d, w0), NOT carrier latitude. Closed form (Vening-Meinesz 1947; Melosh 1977; restated Beuthe 2010 eqs.90-91), TENSILE-POSITIVE convention:
  sigma_theta = -(E/(5+nu))*(df/6)*(3*cos(2*theta) + 5)   [meridional, along great circles through w0]
  sigma_phi   = -(E/(5+nu))*(df/6)*(9*cos(2*theta) - 1)   [azimuthal, around small circles of w0]
where df = f_new - f_old < 0 for despinning (rotational flattening RELAXES as spin slows), E=Young's modulus, nu=Poisson (use 0.25). f = h2T*Omega^2*R/(2g) (Beuthe eq.92), so |df| scales with the drop in Omega^2.
CODEABLE: fold E,nu,df into ONE seeded positive scalar A_despin (>0 because the leading minus times df<0 is positive). Let mu=cos(2*theta):
  sigma_theta_despin = A_despin*(3*mu + 5)/6   // bracket in [2,8] => POSITIVE (tensile) at every latitude
  sigma_phi_despin   = A_despin*(9*mu - 1)/6   // bracket in [-10,+8] => sign flips at mu=1/9
Seed A_despin = DESPIN_REF*(0.6 + 0.8*alea('despin:amp:'+macroSeed)()).
despinStress.sigmaTheta: MERIDIONAL sigma_theta = A_despin*(3*cos2theta+5)/6. Bracket (3*cos2theta+5) runs 2 (paleo-equator, cos2theta=-1) to 8 (paleo-pole, cos2theta=+1); STRICTLY POSITIVE for all theta (verified: min=2>0). => meridional stress is TENSILE EVERYWHERE, strongest at paleo-poles. Drives E-W-striking tension fractures / normal faults in the polar provinces (cracks open perpendicular to the N-S meridional tension).
despinStress.sigmaPhi: AZIMUTHAL sigma_phi = A_despin*(9*cos2theta-1)/6. Bracket (9*cos2theta-1) runs +8 at pole (TENSILE) to -10 at equator (COMPRESSIVE). Sign change where 9*cos2theta-1=0 => cos2theta=1/9 => theta = 0.5*acos(1/9) = 41.81deg colatitude = 48.19deg paleo-LATITUDE. This is the classic ~48deg boundary between despin faulting provinces.
despinStress.signConvention: TENSILE POSITIVE (Beuthe 2010 line: 'Tensile stress is positive'). NOTE the trap: Melosh 1977 himself uses the OPPOSITE convention ('Note that compressive stress is positive', p.225) -- his eq.20 sigma_theta = -5mu(f-f') is NEGATIVE = tensile in his sign. Beuthe re-expressed it tensile-positive (eqs.90-91), which is the convention to use in code so sigma1>0 means tension. Pick ONE convention (tensile-positive) and keep it consistent into the diagonalizer so sigma1>TENSILE_THRESH means tension.
despinStress.tensileVsCompressiveRegions: MERIDIONAL (sigma_theta): tensile at all latitudes, max at poles. AZIMUTHAL (sigma_phi): TENSILE in the two POLAR caps (|paleo-lat|>48.2deg), COMPRESSIVE in the EQUATORIAL belt (|paleo-lat|<48.2deg). Resulting fracture pattern (Melosh 1977; Beuthe 2010): POLAR provinces = E-W-striking normal faults / tension joints (both principal stresses tensile, most-tensile is azimuthal near pole); EQUATORIAL province = strike-slip faults striking ~60deg from north (meridional tensile + azimuthal compressive => max-shear conjugate set). For a lineament writer this means: lineaments form readily in the polar caps; near the equator they trend obliquely (~60deg from the meridian).
despinStress.principalDirections: Despin stress is DIAGONAL in the {theta_hat (toward w0-pole), phi_hat (around w0)} frame -- no shear by symmetry. The most-tensile principal direction: in polar caps it is phi_hat (azimuthal, the larger tensile) so cracks open along meridians and strike E-W; in the equatorial belt the only tensile component is sigma_theta (meridional) so the most-tensile axis is theta_hat and pure-despin cracks would strike E-W there too, but the strong azimuthal COMPRESSION rotates the failure (shear) into the ~60deg-from-north strike-slip set. theta_traj for pure despin = direction of phi_hat or theta_hat depending on which is more tensile at that node.
despinStress.formula_check_value: Verified numerically at nu=0.25: sigma_phi=0 exactly at colatitude 41.81deg (latitude 48.19deg); sigma_theta bracket minimum = 2 (>0, tensile everywhere); at equator sigma_phi/A = -10/6 (compressive), at pole +8/6 (tensile); meridional at pole +8/6, at equator +2/6.

diurnalStress.principalAxisRotation: POSITION-DEPENDENT, TIME-DEPENDENT principal-axis rotation is produced by the NONZERO SHEAR sigma_tp proportional to cos(theta)*[3 sin2phi cos(wt) - 4 f cos2phi sin(wt)]. Because sigma_tp != 0 (off the tidal axes and poles) and its phase (cos wt vs sin wt parts) differs from the normal components' phase, the 2x2 tensor [[sigma_tt, sigma_tp],[sigma_tp, sigma_pp]] has its eigenvectors ROTATE smoothly as wt advances over one orbit. Verified numerically: at a non-degenerate point, theta_principal = 0.5*atan2(2*sigma_tp, sigma_tt - sigma_pp) sweeps through a wide angular range across wt=0..360deg while sigma1 rises and falls. SENSE (Greenberg 2002 / Hoppa 1999): as the tidal bulge migrates, the principal stresses at a fixed point rotate CLOCKWISE in the northern hemisphere and COUNTERCLOCKWISE in the southern hemisphere (the cos(theta) factor in sigma_tp flips sign across the equator, giving the hemispheric sense reversal).
diurnalStress.cycloidEmergence: WHY cycloids fall out free: a tension crack propagates PERPENDICULAR to the most-tensile principal stress (i.e. ALONG theta_traj) whenever sigma1 exceeds the ice tensile strength. Because theta_traj rotates continuously as the diurnal field rotates (above), a SLOWLY propagating crack (a few km/hr -- Hoppa: 2-4 km/hr) continuously re-aims, tracing a CURVING ARC instead of a straight line. When sigma1 drops below the ARREST threshold (Hoppa: 0.4 bar) the crack STALLS. ~One orbit later sigma1 again exceeds the INITIATION threshold (Hoppa: 0.7 bar), but during the stall the principal axis has rotated, so the next segment launches in a NEW direction -- producing the sharp CUSP between arcs. Chain of arcs+cusps = the cycloid. In a render-once writer this emerges automatically: steer the ridged field along theta_traj(d) and gate by sigma1(d); the spatial rotation of theta_traj across the surface (the frozen-phase analog of the temporal rotation) bends the steered ridges into arcs, and the sigma1-gate carves the cusps where tension dips below CREST_THRESH. No crack-walking simulation needed -- the curvature is baked into the theta_traj field.
diurnalStress.parameters: n=mean motion, R=radius, g=surface gravity, e=eccentricity (diurnal amplitude proportional to e), mu=shell rigidity, h2/l2=tidal Love numbers, nu=Poisson(0.33 for ice surface), f=libration factor (=1 pure eccentricity). Numeric scales (Europa): diurnal tensile amplitude ~40-100 kPa (Hoppa: peak ~1 bar=100 kPa, most regions less; Greenberg: ~40 kPa typical); initiation threshold 0.7 bar (70 kPa) or modeled 25 kPa; arrest threshold 0.4 bar (40 kPa) or modeled 15 kPa; propagation speed 2-4 km/hr; cusp spacing 75-150 km; orbital period 3.55 days.

normalization.method: Divide the summed raw stress by a per-body STRESS_REF constant -- EXACTLY the plates.js pattern (plates.js:60 STRESS_REF=1.35, applied at lines 219-220 as clamp(0,1, normalComp/STRESS_REF)). Pipeline: (1) sigma_total(d) = w_despin*sigma_despin(theta_w0) + w_diur*sigma_diur(theta_t,phi_t,phi0), with per-REGIME weights {icy-active: w_despin~1, w_diur~1; volatile-cold: w_despin~1, w_diur~0.15; eyeball-despun: w_despin~1, w_diur=0}; (2) diagonalize each node's 2x2 to get sigma1 (signed max-tensile); (3) normalize sigma1_n = clamp(-1, 1, sigma1 / STRESS_REF). Recommended STRESS_REF method: EMPIRICAL-DETERMINISTIC -- one O(N) reduction pass to find maxAbs = max over nodes of |sigma1_raw|, then STRESS_REF = maxAbs / TARGET with TARGET~0.9. This is byte-deterministic (pure function of the field, NO RNG, NO Date.now) and uses the full [-1,1] range regardless of how the seed scaled A_despin/A_diur. Alternative ANALYTIC method: STRESS_REF = w_despin*A_despin*(10/6) + w_diur*A_diur*PEAK_DIUR (10/6 = the largest despin bracket magnitude); simpler but leaves dynamic-range slack across seeds.
normalization.rationale: The thresholds (TENSILE_THRESH, CHAOS_THRESH, CREST_THRESH) are dimensionless and assume sigma1 lives in ~[-1,1] (tension up to +1, compression to -1). Raw stress is in arbitrary seeded units -- A_despin and A_diur absorb E, df, eccentricity e, rigidity mu, and Love numbers, none of which the threshold gate should depend on. Normalizing by STRESS_REF decouples threshold tuning from physical-amplitude seeding, exactly as plates.js divides relative-motion normal stress by STRESS_REF so UPLIFT_GAIN/RIFT_GAIN thresholds are seed-independent. The empirical-deterministic variant additionally guarantees every body uses its full dynamic range, so a low-amplitude seed still produces gated lineaments rather than an all-sub-threshold (blank) field.
normalization.mapsTo: sigma1_n in [-1,1]: +1 = strongest tension in this body (most likely to crack), 0 = neutral, -1 = strongest compression (gated OUT of lineament formation). TENSILE_THRESH ~ 0.0-0.2 (only tensile nodes form lineaments); CHAOS_THRESH high (>~0.6, where icy-active shells go to chaos/disruption); CREST_THRESH on the steered RIDGED field R[i] (separate from sigma1, see crestRule).

diagonalization.thetaFormula: theta_traj = 0.5 * atan2(2*b, a - c)  -- VERIFIED CORRECT for M=[[a,b],[b,c]]. Returns the angle (from local east/+x toward north/+y) of the eigenVECTOR of the LARGER (most-tensile, since tensile-positive) eigenvalue. ARGUMENT ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: atan2(y = 2*b, x = a - c). Off-by-90 traps (both verified to fail): (1) atan2(2*b, c - a) (denominator sign flipped) returns the SMALLER-eigenvalue axis => theta_traj rotated exactly 90deg => lineaments steer along the COMPRESSIVE axis -- silently plausible, fails the AC. (2) atan(2*b/(a-c)) loses the full-circle branch and is undefined at a==c. Because theta_traj is written to carrier.grainAngle AND is the steering axis AND is tested, a 90deg error is self-consistent across all three uses and fails SILENTLY. Guard: after computing theta_traj, assert the (cos,sin) axis maximizes the Rayleigh quotient n^T M n (i.e. equals lambda_max within eps); if not, add pi/2.
diagonalization.eigenvalueFormula:
lambda_max = (a+c)/2 + sqrt(((a-c)/2)^2 + b^2)   [= sigma1, SIGNED max-tensile principal stress, feeds the tensile gate]
lambda_min = (a+c)/2 - sqrt(((a-c)/2)^2 + b^2)   [most-compressive principal stress]
VERIFIED: 20000 random symmetric 2x2 matrices, max |analytic - numpy.linalg.eigh| eigenvalue error = 7.1e-15; theta=0.5*atan2(2b,a-c) aligned with the larger eigenvalue's eigenvector in 20000/20000 cases (max 1-|cos angle| = 3.3e-16). sigma1 is SIGNED: at a node where both principal stresses are compressive, lambda_max < 0 and is correctly gated OUT of lineament formation.
diagonalization.thetaFormula_check: off-by-90 trap demonstrated for [[3,1],[1,-1]]: correct theta=13.28deg points along the lambda_max=3.24 eigenvector (0.973,0.230); the sign-flipped denominator gives 76.72deg (90deg off, the lambda_min axis).
diagonalization.notes: Tangent-frame mapping: a = sigma_ee (east-east), b = sigma_en (east-north shear), c = sigma_nn (north-north), in the LOCAL frame {east,north}=carrier.tangentFrameAt(d). Build a,b,c by: (i) evaluating despin principal stresses in the {theta_w0, phi_w0} frame and rotating into {east,north}; (ii) evaluating diurnal sigma_tt,sigma_pp,sigma_tp in the {theta_t,phi_t} frame and rotating into {east,north}; (iii) summing the two 2x2 tensors component-wise. Rotation of a 2x2 stress tensor by angle psi between frames: standard R(psi)^T M R(psi). theta_traj is reported in the {east,north} frame (consistent with carrier.grainAngle).

crestRule.rule: lineamentNode[i] (Uint8) = 1 if and only if ( R[i] > CREST_THRESH ) AND ( sigma1_n[i] > TENSILE_THRESH ). R[i] is the steered ridged field (a ridged-multifractal / abs-of-signed-noise sampled along theta_traj, in [0,1] after its own normalization). It is a pure ABSOLUTE-THRESHOLD test on a continuous field, gated by the (normalized, signed) max-tensile stress -- NOT a comparison of R[i] to its graph neighbours. Suggested constants: CREST_THRESH ~ 0.62 (ridge-shoulder fraction of the ridged field), TENSILE_THRESH ~ 0.05 (just-tensile). The ridged field is constructed so its narrow high-value ridge lines sit where cracks are; the threshold slices those ridge lines into the discrete crack set.
crestRule.whyThresholdNotLocalMax: A relative LOCAL-MAX rule -- 'R[i] is a crack if R[i] > R[j] for all graph-neighbours j' -- is FRAGILE on an irregular sphere graph for three reasons. (1) ADJACENCY-ORDER dependence: the neighbour set adj[i] varies with mesh construction; a node with 5 vs 6 neighbours has a different chance of being declared a max, so the lineament set changes with mesh topology even at the same resolution. (2) FLOAT-EQUALITY fragility: on plateaus or near-flat ridge crests, R[i]==R[j] within float epsilon makes 'strictly greater' nondeterministic w.r.t. tie-breaking / iteration order, breaking the byte-identical-determinism hard rule. (3) RESOLUTION dependence: refining the mesh adds nodes between former maxima, so the count and placement of local maxima drifts -- the same body at the 600-node test carrier vs the ~40k lab mesh yields different cracks. A THRESHOLD rule R[i]>CREST_THRESH is ORDER-INDEPENDENT (each node decided in isolation, no neighbour reads, no iteration-order sensitivity) and RESOLUTION-INDEPENDENT (CREST_THRESH is a level-set on a continuous field; refining the mesh samples the SAME level set more densely, giving the same crack curves at higher fidelity rather than a different set). This mirrors plates.js using an angular BELT_RADIANS level/falloff (resolution-independent) rather than a fixed hop count.

uncertainties: GROUND-TRUTH SOURCE QUALITY: the Melosh 1977 and Beuthe arXiv PDFs were extracted via pypdf and the OCR was noisy (e.g. Melosh's text rendered '48' as '55' in one spot for the incompressible limit). I cross-verified the despin closed form against Beuthe 2010 eqs.90-91 (clean LaTeX text) and computed the critical latitude myself (48.19deg at nu=0.25), so the despin math is solid. But the EXACT Melosh equation numbers (19-21) coefficients are reconstructed from messy OCR -- trust the Beuthe restatement (eqs.90-91) over my Melosh quotes.

MELOSH CRITICAL LATITUDE: Melosh's own text (incompressible limit) says azimuthal stress is compressive 'up to 55deg latitude'; Beuthe's general thin-shell result at nu=0.25 gives 48.2deg latitude (cos2theta=1/9). The 48deg figure is the standard modern value and what I used; the discrepancy is Melosh's incompressible (nu=0.5) special case vs general nu. If you need the exact crossover for a chosen nu, solve 9cos2theta-1=0 is nu-independent in Beuthe's eq.91 form -- but the FULL (variable-thickness) pseudo-node moves with nu (Beuthe quotes 65.9deg colat for the variable-thickness P2 term). For constant-thickness use latitude 48.2deg.

DIURNAL TENSOR SIMPLIFICATION: the membrane eq.146 has full Love-number (h2,l2) and libration (f) structure. The pseudocode collapses b1=b2=g1=g2=g3=1 for illustration, which makes sigma_tt==sigma_pp at each instant (degenerate) -- in that special case the principal axis jumps rather than rotates smoothly. For REAL cycloid curvature you MUST use distinct beta/gamma (i.e. A != 0 via h2/l2 != 3, Beuthe eq.66): set e.g. b1=4,b2=-2,g1=0,g2=2,g3=1 (verified to give smooth theta_traj sweep). I left placeholder 1's in the pseudocode for clarity -- engineers should plug real beta/gamma from chosen Love numbers, or hand-pick distinct values per regime.

PRINCIPAL-AXIS ROTATION SENSE: the CW-north/CCW-south sense is from Greenberg 2002 (paraphrased via search, the review is paywalled -- I could not read the primary text directly). The mechanism (cos(theta) sign flip across the equator in sigma_tp) is consistent with it and verified in the membrane eq.146 form, but the exact sense convention should be spot-checked against a Europa cycloid figure before shipping.

DOUBLE-RIDGE CROSS-SECTION: the analytic trough+shoulder profile (Gaussian trough at center, two Gaussian shoulders) is a PLAUSIBLE-MORPHOLOGY model matching observed Europa double-ridge cross-sections (central trough flanked by two raised flanks), NOT a derived elastic-flexure solution. The widths (0.25, 0.22) and heights (RIDGE_DEPTH, SHOULDER_HT) are tunable art constants, not physical. If physical fidelity matters, the literature models double ridges via flexural uplift / shear-heating diapirism -- out of scope for this stress-field task.

STEERING DIRECTION SIGN: I steer the ridged field by sampling noise along the crack-NORMAL (-sin th, cos th) so ridge lines run ALONG theta_traj. Whether ridges should run along theta_traj (the most-tensile axis = the direction a crack OPENS perpendicular to, so the crack LINE is perpendicular to the most-tensile stress) needs one definitional check: a tension crack strikes PERPENDICULAR to the most-tensile principal stress. So if theta_traj is the most-tensile AXIS, the crack LINE should run perpendicular to theta_traj. Verify this 90deg choice against a known despin pattern (polar E-W cracks) before locking -- it is the same off-by-90 family as the diagonalizer trap.

REGIME WEIGHTS + THRESHOLDS: w_despin/w_diur per regime and the threshold constants (TENSILE_THRESH 0.05, CHAOS_THRESH/CREST_THRESH 0.62) are starting points matched to the plates.js tuning philosophy, not calibrated. They need a sweep against the AC structure bars (analogous to plates.js AC2) on real seeds.

stressSkeptics.focus: despin-membrane-stress-closed-form-and-sign-convention (Melosh 1977 / Beuthe 2010): tensile/compressive pattern and the two principal components
issues: PRINCIPAL-DIRECTION ERROR (real, but prose-only): The spec's `principalDirections` field says 'in polar caps it is phi_hat (azimuthal, the larger tensile)' and `tensileVsCompressiveRegions` says 'most-tensile is azimuthal near pole'. This is FALSE. Algebraically sigma_theta - sigma_phi = ((3cos2t+5) - (9cos2t-1))/6 = (1 - cos2t) = 2*sin^2(theta) >= 0 EVERYWHERE, equal to zero only exactly AT the pole. So the MERIDIONAL component (theta_hat) is the most-tensile principal axis at every latitude; azimuthal (phi_hat) is never strictly the larger tensile. This contradicts the spec's own numerics (sigma_theta=1.326 vs sigma_phi=1.311 at 5deg colatitude) and both primary sources: Melosh 1977 eq.21 ('sigma_phi is always larger than sigma_theta' in his COMPRESSIVE-positive convention => meridional is more TENSILE) and Beuthe 2010 Sec.5.3 ('the meridional stress is more extensional - or less compressive - than the azimuthal stress').

DOWNSTREAM RISK from that error: the spec's pseudocode diagonalizes the summed numeric tensor and selects lamMax by formula, so the codepath is NOT corrupted. But the steering rationale and the despin-only 'theta_traj = phi_hat in polar caps' prose, if hand-implemented, would steer the polar-cap lineaments ~90deg wrong. The strike CONCLUSION (E-W cracks in polar caps) still happens to be right because the two stresses are nearly equal near the pole, but the stated reason (azimuthal dominates) is wrong; the meridional N-S tension is what opens the E-W cracks.

MINOR IMPRECISION in `uncertainties`: the Melosh-55deg vs Beuthe-48deg azimuthal-sign-change discrepancy is attributed to 'Melosh incompressible (nu=0.5) special case vs general nu.' The cleaner attribution (Beuthe 2010 p.5) is HYDROSTATIC flattening (Melosh's thin-shell example, bracket (1-3cos2theta) -> 54.7deg) vs MEMBRANE Love-number flattening with ratio l2T/h2T=(1+nu)/(5+nu) (Beuthe/Matsuyama-Nimmo, bracket (9cos2theta-1) -> 48.2deg). The 48.2deg boundary is genuinely nu-INDEPENDENT (no nu in the zeroth-order bracket, only in the 1/(5+nu) prefactor). Does not affect the chosen formula.

PREFACTOR (non-issue, noting for completeness): the spec's brackets are (3cos2t+5)/6 and (9cos2t-1)/6, while Beuthe's exact zeroth-order brackets are (3cos2t+5)/4 and (9cos2t-1)/4. They differ by a common 3/2 factor that is fully absorbed into the seeded scalar A_despin, so the relative shape, sign pattern, component ratio, and critical latitude are all preserved. Correct as used.

stressSkeptics.focus: diurnal-tidal-stress and whether the stated position-dependent principal-axis rotation actually produces curving/chaining cycloids (Hoppa et al. 1999)
issues: ROTATION-SENSE IS BACKWARDS (the headline diurnal claim). The spec states: 'the principal stresses at a fixed point rotate CLOCKWISE in the northern hemisphere and COUNTERCLOCKWISE in the southern hemisphere' and attributes this to Greenberg 2002 / Hoppa 1999. The primary literature says the OPPOSITE for the DIURNAL tide. The canonical statement, attributed directly to Hoppa et al. 1999b and repeated in Greenberg 2002 and the cycloid-cusp literature, is: 'The orientation of each principal component of the DIURNAL stress at every point on the surface rotates 180 deg each europan day with a COUNTER-CLOCKWISE rotational sense in the NORTHERN hemisphere and CLOCKWISE in the SOUTHERN hemisphere.' Verified across 4+ independent sources. The spec appears to have grabbed the NON-SYNCHRONOUS-ROTATION (NSR) bulge-migration sense (which IS clockwise-north, per the HIIPS Greenberg-tectonics page: 'clockwise rotation of the stress direction with time... consistent with migration due to non-synchronous rotation') and mislabeled it as the diurnal sense. NSR and diurnal are different phenomena with OPPOSITE senses; the spec fused them.

DELIVERED PSEUDOCODE IS FUNCTIONALLY BROKEN for its own headline mechanism. The build-ready shellRelief.js block ships the diurnal coefficients inline as b1=b2=g1=g2=g3=1 (lines: 'const Stt_r=...; const Spp_r=Stt_r, Spp_i=Stt_i; // equal here'). I verified numerically: with these placeholders sigma_tt === sigma_pp at EVERY phase, so the 2x2 tensor is [[s, s_tp],[s_tp, s]] and its principal axis does NOT rotate smoothly -- it SNAPS between exactly +45 and -45 deg as the shear sigma_tp changes sign. No continuous re-aiming => no curving arcs => no cycloids. The prose ('theta_principal sweeps through a wide angular range across wt=0..360') describes the DISTINCT-parameter case, but the code as written is the DEGENERATE case. An engineer copy-pasting the pseudocode gets two snapping orientations, not cycloids. (The spec flags this in uncertainty #3, but the fix is NOT in the shipped code -- it remains a latent build-breaker.)

MECHANISM-VS-GEOMETRY CONFLATION (caveat the spec under-flags). The real Hoppa cycloid curvature is TEMPORAL: theta_traj rotates at a FIXED point as a crack slowly walks (2-4 km/hr) across an orbit; the crack tip integrates a time-varying stress direction. The spec substitutes SPATIAL variation of theta_traj at ONE frozen phase ('the frozen-phase analog of the temporal rotation'). These are NOT the same curve. A render-once spatial steering field produces cycloid-LIKE arcs, not the physically-traced cycloid geometry (which needs crack-position x time coupling). The spec discloses 'no crack-walking simulation needed' but oversells with 'cycloids fall out free' / 'the curvature is baked into the theta_traj field' -- the output is a visual analog, not a Hoppa cycloid.
corrections: FIX THE ROTATION SENSE: For the DIURNAL eccentricity tide, principal stress rotates COUNTERCLOCKWISE in the NORTHERN hemisphere, CLOCKWISE in the SOUTHERN, 180 deg per orbit (Hoppa et al. 1999b; Greenberg et al. 2002 Rev. Geophys.). Reserve the clockwise-north sense for the NSR/long-term bulge-migration field if that is ever added. Source for diurnal sense: Groenleer/Kattenhorn-type cusp-angle papers and Hurford obliquity-cycloid paper all quote Hoppa 1999b verbatim; e.g. 'rotates 180 deg each europan day with a counter-clockwise rotational sense in the northern hemisphere and clockwise in the southern hemisphere.' Practical effect on output: in the code the cos(theta) factor in sigma_tp already produces a hemispheric sign flip across the equator, so the GEOMETRY of the flip is correct -- but the documented sense LABEL and any hand-tuned arc-concavity convention must be swapped. Cross-check before shipping: 'cycloids that grow E->W are concave toward the equator; W->E are concave toward the pole' (same in both hemispheres) -- use this observable as the acceptance check.

REMOVE THE DEGENERATE COEFFICIENTS FROM THE SHIPPED CODE, not just the uncertainties note. Replace the inline b1=b2=g1=g2=g3=1 with a non-degenerate set tied to Beuthe eqs.63-66: with A=2 (the ELASTIC limit Europa value, Beuthe states A=2 in the elastic limit, line ~1688), (b1,b2)=(A+3,A-3)=(5,-1), (g1,g2)=(A-1,A+1)=(1,3), g3=1. (The spec's suggested b1=4,b2=-2,g1=0,g2=2 corresponds to A=1, which is internally consistent and non-degenerate but is NOT the physical elastic value -- prefer A=2.) Then sigma_tt != sigma_pp and the principal axis rotates smoothly (verified: sweeps the full range over wt=0..360). This is mandatory, not optional, for any cycloid output.

VERIFIED CORRECT (keep): (a) The diurnal stress formulas sigma_tt/sigma_pp/sigma_tp transcribe Beuthe 2016 eq.146 EXACTLY -- including sigma_tp = -3(n^2 R/g) e g3 cos(theta)(3 sin2phi + 4 i f cos2phi); the eccentricity potential (eq.143) is purely P20+P22 with NO P21, so dropping the m=1 sin(theta)*(phi) shear term is correct for a zero-obliquity eccentricity tide. (b) A = ((1+nu)/(1-nu))(h2/l2 - 3) matches Beuthe eq.66; (b1,b2)=ul2(A+3,A-3), (g1,g2)=ul2(A-1,A+1), g3=ul2 match eqs.63-65 exactly. (c) The cos(theta) factor genuinely flips sign across the tidal-frame equator, so the hemispheric-reversal MECHANISM is real (only the verbal CW/CCW label is wrong). (d) Hoppa thresholds verified verbatim from the primary source: initiation 0.7 bar, arrest 0.4 bar, speed 2-4 km/hr, cusp spacing 75-150 km, max diurnal tensile ~1 bar, period ~85 hr (3.55 d), crack propagates perpendicular to max tensile stress and cusps form because the field reorients during the stall. (e) The diagonalizer theta_traj=0.5*atan2(2b,a-c) and the smooth spatial variation of theta_traj at a frozen phase are numerically correct.

MINOR: 'f=1 for pure eccentricity tide' is mislabeled. Per Beuthe eq.145, f = 1 - (gs/2e)e^{i psi}; f=1 means NO forced libration (gs=0), not 'pure eccentricity'. The value is a fine default but the rationale text is imprecise. ALSO: the alternative modeled thresholds '25 kPa initiation / 15 kPa arrest' (attributed to Hurford et al. 2009) could NOT be independently verified -- that PDF was inaccessible; treat as unconfirmed rather than authoritative.

stressSkeptics.focus: normalization, symmetric 2x2 diagonalization (theta=0.5*atan2(2b,a-c); eigenvalues (a+c)/2 +/- sqrt(((a-c)/2)^2+b^2)), and threshold crest rule (order/resolution independence)
issues: DIAGONALIZATION off-by-90 trap #1 is MATHEMATICALLY WRONG. Spec claims atan2(2*b, c-a) (flipped denominator) 'returns the SMALLER-eigenvalue axis => theta_traj rotated exactly 90deg => steers along the COMPRESSIVE axis.' It does not. Identity: atan2(2b,-(a-c)) = pi - atan2(2b,a-c), so 0.5*that = pi/2 - theta_correct, i.e. a REFLECTION of the correct axis about the 45deg line, NOT a +90deg rotation. Verified: the flipped axis coincides with NEITHER principal axis in 49959/50000 random cases. The spec's worked example is also wrong: for [[3,1],[1,-1]] it gives 76.72deg and calls that 'the lambda_min axis', but the Rayleigh quotient at 76.72deg is -0.34, which is neither lamMax(=3.236) nor lamMin(=-1.236). The angular difference in that example is 63.43deg, not 90deg, exactly because it is a reflection not a rotation.

DIAGONALIZATION guard does not defend against the bug the spec warns about. The Rayleigh guard 'if(rq<mean) th+=PI/2' correctly rescues a GENUINE +90deg error (verified 50000/50000), but it does NOT rescue the flipped-denominator reflection bug (rescues only 50/50000). So an engineer who follows the spec's incorrect trap description, writes the flipped denominator, and trusts the guard, ships a silently-broken steering field. The guard is fine for its real purpose; the spec mislabels the failure mode it protects against.

NORMALIZATION dynamic-range / mapsTo wording is imprecise (not a hard math error, but misleading for tuning). Empirical-deterministic STRESS_REF = max_i|sigma1|/TARGET maps the largest-MAGNITUDE node to +/-0.9, NOT the most-tensile node to +1. When compression dominates (which is the case in the despin equatorial belt: sigma_phi=-10/6 vs max tension +8/6), the tension side only reaches +TARGET*(8/10)=+0.72 and never +0.9. So 'mapsTo: +1 = strongest tension in this body' and rationale 'every body uses its full dynamic range' are inaccurate for compression-dominated fields; TENSILE_THRESH then sits on a tension axis whose scale is set by a compressive global extremum.

CREST-RULE resolution-independence is partially undercut by the RECOMMENDED normalizer. The crest rule correctly argues CREST_THRESH on R is a mesh-independent level set (valid: R is a continuous function of position). BUT the co-gate TENSILE_THRESH operates on sigma1_n = sigma1 / STRESS_REF, and the spec's RECOMMENDED STRESS_REF is the EMPIRICAL max_i|sigma1|, which is a sampled extremum that drifts with resolution (verified: despin sigma1 max sampled at 1.238 for N=42 vs 1.333 for N=40962, true sup 1.3333). A fixed physical point's sigma1_n therefore changes with mesh density and its TENSILE_THRESH crossing can move, so the lineament gate is NOT strictly resolution-independent under the recommended method. The spec's own ANALYTIC STRESS_REF alternative (no per-node reduction) IS resolution-independent. The crest-rule section's blanket resolution-independence claim is in tension with the normalization section's recommended choice.
corrections: Off-by-90 trap #1: replace the false claim with the correct math. atan2(2b, c-a) computes theta_flip = 90deg - theta_correct (a REFLECTION about the 45deg line), NOT theta_correct + 90deg and NOT the compressive/minor axis. It equals a principal axis only in degenerate cases (b~0 or a~c). The genuinely dangerous mistakes are: (a) writing th = correct + 90 (a true rotation onto the minor/compressive axis), and (b) the reflection from flipping the denominator. Keep the Rayleigh guard but state clearly it only rescues case (a); case (b) needs a code-level check that the denominator argument is (a-c) not (c-a). Drop the worked-example assertion that 76.72deg is 'the lambda_min axis'.

Strengthen the guard to a true principal-axis assertion: after computing th, verify BOTH that rq(th) == lamMax AND that the orthogonal axis rq(th+90) == lamMin within eps; if only the first is patched by +90 but the orthogonal does not match lamMin, the angle is a reflection (bug b) and must be recomputed, not nudged. A simple robust alternative immune to both traps: build the unit eigenvector directly as v = normalize([b, lamMax - a]) (or [lamMax - c, b]), with the isotropic fallback when |b| and |a-c| are both < eps.

Normalization wording: change 'mapsTo: +1 = strongest tension' to '+/-0.9 (=TARGET) is reached by the strongest-MAGNITUDE principal stress; the tension side reaches +TARGET only when tension is the global magnitude extremum, otherwise less.' If the intent is that the most-tensile node maps to +1, normalize by max_i(sigma1) (signed max over tensile nodes), not by max_i|sigma1|; but then compression is not symmetrically scaled. Pick explicitly based on whether the tensile gate or the compressive gate needs the calibrated end.

Resolution-independence: if strict mesh-invariance of the lineament set is an AC, use the ANALYTIC STRESS_REF (= w_despin*A_despin*(10/6) + w_diur*A_diur*PEAK_DIUR) rather than the empirical max-reduction, since the analytic constant is a pure function of the seeded amplitudes and does not sample the mesh. If the empirical method is kept for dynamic-range reasons, document that the tensile gate is only ASYMPTOTICALLY resolution-independent (converges as the mesh resolves the stress extremum) and that low-res test carriers (e.g. 600 nodes) will differ slightly from the ~40k lab mesh.

thinSpots.gap: Gas giants, hot-Jupiters, Saturnian and ice-giant (Neptunian) bodies — 4 archetypes — have NO relief writer in the world-engine, ever. They have no solid surface, so there is no carrier.height to REPLACE. Their entire visual identity IS the E5 atmospheric band/jet/storm field. But the ROADMAP routes all four archetypes' whole identity through ONE sub-field of ONE increment (#3, E5 climate), and within that, the great-spot / storm-train / polar-vortex PLACEMENT (features F27/F28/F29) is undesigned. In the live code, placement is currently a "bag of overlays": PlanetGenerator.js:587-655 rolls storm positions with rng.range at a RANDOM latitude (phi=acos(rng.range(-0.7,0.7))) and the lab cards F27/F28/F29 hash-place spots — uncorrelated with the band/jet field they sit in. That is exactly the divorced-from-history pattern the program exists to kill. A zonal band field does NOT by itself emit vortices; placement needs its own deterministic, physically-grounded model.
thinSpots.restatement: Build a deterministic vortex-placement model (great-spot / storm-train / polar-vortex) for a no-surface body, following the proven plates.js writer pattern (seeded field -> classify -> write carrier fields -> bounded relax -> regime gate) but adapted to a fluid envelope. Since there is no height to REPLACE, the writer produces a ZONAL-FLOW + CLOUD-ALBEDO + SHEAR field on the carrier, and — critically — derives storm/vortex placement AS A CONSEQUENCE of that jet field (vortices live in the anticyclonic shear zones BETWEEN jets, pinned to specific latitudes), not as an independent random sprinkle. Keyed off rotation (D8), internal heat / convective vigor (D12 + T_eq D1), gravity/radius (D14), and tidal lock (D7, for hot-Jupiters). Slot it as a scoped sub-increment of #3 (E5).
thinSpots.recommendedApproach:
RECOMMENDED: "Jet-lattice -> shear-zone -> vortex" writer (call it `gasFlow.js`), a sibling three-free writer in src/worldengine/base that runs as sub-increment 3b, AFTER the E5 zonal band/jet field (3a) computes the jet profile. It mirrors plates.js stage-for-stage:

1. SEED THE JET LATTICE (analog of plate centroids). Compute jet count N_jets deterministically from the Rhines scale: the jet half-width scales as L_R ~ sqrt(2U/beta) where beta = 2*Omega*cos(lat)/R, so N_jets per hemisphere ~ proportional to rotation rate Omega and radius R, divided by wind speed. Codeable closed form anchored to real bodies: njetsPerHemi = clamp(round(K * (radiusEarth/rotationHours) * vigorFactor), 1, 14), calibrated so Jovian(R=11.2,rot=9.9h)->~13-15 total jets, Saturnian(9.4,10.7h)->~11, Neptunian(3.9,16.1h)->~3 (matches observed ~20-30 jets gas / ~3 ice). This reproduces and REPLACES the lab's existing bandCount=clamp(round(12*radiusEarth/rotationHours),3,16) but now as the shared upstream the vortex stage reads. Jet latitudes phi_j placed at equal sin(lat) intervals (equal-area), with a wide prograde equatorial superrotation jet at lat 0 always present. Per-jet sign alternates prograde/retrograde; a seeded jitter (alea 'gas:jets:'+seed) perturbs amplitudes/widths so worlds differ.

2. WRITE THE ZONAL-FLOW FIELD + CLASSIFY SHEAR (analog of Voronoi partition + boundary classification). At each carrier node, evaluate u(lat) = sum of alternating-sign Gaussians on the jet latitudes (the analytic zonal wind profile). The shear du/dlat classifies every latitude band: ANTICYCLONIC shear zone (where vortices are favored) vs CYCLONIC, exactly as the plates writer classifies convergent/divergent/transform from relative-motion stress. Write carrier.grainAngle = local jet direction (azimuthal, the "grain" of the flow), carrier.grainMag = |u(lat)| (jet strength), carrier.faultDensity = |du/dlat| (shear intensity — the storm-favorability field, the direct analog of boundaryStress/faultDensity in plates.js where faultDensity = |boundaryStress|). Write carrier.height = signed cloud-altitude/albedo scalar: + (bright zone, anticyclonic upwelling) where u-curvature is anticyclonic, - (dark belt, cyclonic subsidence) — the luminance alternation that IS the visible band. (height is repurposed as cloud-deck signed altitude/albedo, NOT terrain; documented as the no-surface substitution.)

3. PLACE VORTICES IN THE ANTICYCLONIC SHEAR ZONES (analog of uplift HIGH at convergent boundaries). This is the architectural fix: the great spot and storm train do NOT get random latitudes; they SNAP to the anticyclonic shear band(s) the jet field just produced. Pick the dominant anticyclonic shear zone (max |du/dlat| with anticyclonic sign, in the |lat|<60 deg active region) -> that is the great-spot latitude (Jovian GRS at ~22S sits between a westward jet at ~20S and eastward at ~26S; >90% of Jovian spots are anticyclonic, all at "the first anticyclonic shear zone away from the equator"). Great spot = the single largest vortex (storms[0]). Storm train = N same-latitude ovals on the next-strongest anticyclonic zone at quasi-regular longitudes (Jupiter's string-of-pearls). Longitudes seeded via alea 'gas:vortex:'+seed. E-W aspect (1.5-2.5) set BY the ambient meridional shear (ovals are stretched by the jet). Vortex count + size scale with convective vigor (internal heat D12 + condensable supply): high vigor -> more, larger spots.

4. POLAR VORTEX = vortex-crystal lattice (analog: a special ring partition at the pole). The number of circumpolar cyclones M is set by anticyclonic shielding / vortex-crystal packing: M ~ round(2*pi*r_ring / (cyclone_spacing)) where cyclone diameter is ~5.5-7 deg latitude and the ring sits at colatitude ~8-10 deg (80-82 deg lat). Jupiter: 5 (S) / 8 (N) + 1 central; Saturn: a wavenumber-6 Rossby-wave meander of the circumpolar jet -> polygonal jet contour r(theta)=r0*(1+a*cos(M*theta)). Variant chosen by vigor: high (Jovian) -> cyclone-lattice; mid (Saturnian) -> polygonal jet; low (ice) -> single lobed cap. M deterministic from r0 (itself from rotation + cyclone deformation radius).

5. BOUNDED RELAX (identical discipline to plates.js): a fixed RELAX_PASSES (~4) Jacobi smooth over carrier.adj on the height/albedo field so band edges read as fluid/festooned, not ruler-straight — convex combination, cannot expand bounds, NOT time-stepping, no while-loop.

6. REGIME GATE: the writer fires only for isGasEnvelope regimes {gas-giant, hot-jupiter, sub-neptune-hazy, Saturnian/Neptunian}; returns before any code for solid bodies (checked FIRST, like plates' isEarthlikePlatePath), so it never clobbers the plate/despun/magmatism paths.

HOT-JUPITER SPECIALIZATION (D7 tidal-lock branch inside the same writer): a tidally locked hot-Jupiter has essentially ONE broad equatorial superrotating jet, no rich banding; the "storm" is the dayside thermal hotspot offset EASTWARD of the substellar point by the Coriolis/Kelvin-Rossby wave dynamics. So when D7 (tidalLock) is set, collapse N_jets->1 (equatorial), and place a single bright hotspot vortex at the equator, longitude = substellar + a deterministic eastward offset (function of rotation/wind, ~10-60 deg east). This reuses stages 2-3 with the jet count forced to 1.
thinSpots.fieldsWritten: NO surface height to REPLACE (gas giant has no surface). The writer REPLACES the carrier fields with an atmospheric reinterpretation, written with `=` (REPLACE), not `+=`, exactly like plates.js writes U: (1) carrier.height = signed CLOUD-DECK ALTITUDE / ALBEDO scalar — bright anticyclonic zones positive, dark cyclonic belts negative (the luminance alternation that is the visible band; documented as repurposed-from-terrain). (2) carrier.grainAngle = local ZONAL JET DIRECTION (azimuthal flow grain) — directly reuses the existing grain-vector channel; the band/jet "fabric." (3) carrier.grainMag = jet strength |u(lat)|. (4) carrier.faultDensity = SHEAR INTENSITY |du/dlat| — the storm-favorability field; exact analog of plates.js setting faultDensity = |boundaryStress|. PLUS a returned diagnostics bundle (not a carrier per-node field, mirroring plates.js returning {centroids, plateCount,...}): jetLats[], jetSigns[], shearZones[] (lat + anticyclonic flag), and the placed vortices array {center:[x,y,z], angularRadius, aspect, rotStrength, mode, latLocked} for great spot (idx 0), storm train (idx 1..k), and polar {sides, M, r0, mode}. These feed the already-reserved uStormPosSize[8]/uStormParams[8]/uStormColor[8]/uStormCount shader carriage and the orphaned polarStorm contract, so the lab's VERIFIED F24-F29 renderers consume a HISTORY-DERIVED placement instead of the current random hash.
thinSpots.deterministicMechanism: Every random draw via alea(seedString) keyed off integer macroSeed, in a DISJOINT 'gas:' namespace (gas:jets:, gas:vortex:, gas:polar:) so it never shares a stream with 'plates:', 'e6:', or the despun writer's 'shell:'. No Math.random, no Date.now anywhere. Same (drivers, macroSeed) -> byte-identical fields (clone the plates.js AC1 no-RNG static-source guard). The deterministic chain: (a) jet count/latitudes are a CLOSED-FORM function of (D8 rotation, D14 radius, vigor) via the Rhines scale — deterministic, no RNG; alea only jitters amplitudes/widths within bounds. (b) shear classification is a pure function of the analytic u(lat) -> du/dlat. (c) vortex LATITUDES are deterministically SELECTED (argmax of anticyclonic shear in the active region), not drawn — RNG only sets longitudes and within-bound size/aspect. (d) polar M is a closed form from r0 and cyclone deformation radius. (e) the only iteration is the fixed RELAX_PASSES Jacobi smooth — bounded, a convex combination, NOT a convergence loop or time-step. This makes placement a deterministic CONSEQUENCE of the physics drivers, which is what makes it reproducible AND history-coherent.
thinSpots.architecturalFit: Fits the writer family exactly and KILLS the "bag of unrelated overlays" rather than adding to it. The core fix: today's storm placement (PlanetGenerator.js random latitude; F27/F28/F29 hash placement) is divorced from the band field — a sticker pasted on. The recommended model makes the band/jet field the SHARED UPSTREAM and derives every vortex FROM it: a great spot is not "a random oval" but "the vortex that forms in this world's dominant anticyclonic shear zone, at the latitude the jet structure dictates, elongated by the ambient shear." That is the same move plates.js makes (mountains are not random highs — they are the consequence of where convergent boundaries fall). Stage-for-stage isomorphism with the proven template: jet-lattice (centroids) -> zonal-flow field + shear classify (Voronoi + boundary classify) -> vortices in anticyclonic zones (uplift at convergent boundaries) -> REPLACE carrier fields -> bounded Jacobi relax -> regime gate. Three-free by construction (imports only alea + simplex-noise + mathutil helpers; never imports three), headless-testable in src/worldengine/base. Sibling writer: the regime gate returns before any code on solid bodies, so it never touches the plate/despun/magmatism carrier writes (zero clobber). Consumes the SAME driver bundle signature as the writer family. Feeds the ALREADY-RESERVED uStorm* shader carriage and the orphaned polarStorm data contract, so the lab's VERIFIED_PENDING_MAX F24-F29 renderers light up with history-derived input — no new render path. One subtlety to flag: unlike a solid body where the band IS the fallback being removed, here the band is the legitimate signal; AC must prove vortices are SHEAR-ZONE-PINNED (placement correlates with the anticyclonic shear field), not latitude-random, to confirm the overlay-divorce is actually fixed.
thinSpots.whichIncrement: Sub-increment 3b ("E5 vortex & storm placement"), a scoped sub-increment INSIDE increment 3 (E5 atmosphere/climate field), running immediately AFTER the E5 zonal band/jet field (3a). It must be its own scoped sub-increment, NOT assumed to fall out of the band field — this is the explicit finding of ROADMAP thin-spot #1. Recommend it be named and contracted separately (its own intent.md + contract.json) even though it ships within the #3 envelope, because it has its own structure ACs (shear-zone pinning) distinct from the band-field ACs.
thinSpots.dependencies: Hard dependency on 3a (the E5 zonal band/jet field) — the vortex stage READS the jet profile u(lat)/shear to place storms; without it there is nothing to pin to (that is the whole point). In the live lab, F24 (zonal belts) + F25 (jets & shear) ALREADY exist as VERIFIED_PENDING_MAX and the jet profile u(phi) is already computed in F25's build (sin(2*pi*bandCoordBase) + equatorial Gaussian); 3b formalizes that into a three-free base/ writer and adds the shear-zone-derived placement. Soft dependency on the plates.js POC as the PATTERN template (already shipped + UAT'd). Depends on D8 (rotation), D1 (T_eq -> contrast/vigor), D12 (tidalHeating -> convective vigor; already surfaced + adapted per the ROADMAP stale-spine correction), D14 (massGravity/radius), and D7 (tidalLock) for the hot-Jupiter branch — all already in the driver bundle. Reserved shader carriage uStormPosSize/Params/Color[8] + uStormCount and the orphaned polarStorm contract already exist (no new uniforms needed). Independent of increments #1 (despun), #4 (magmatism), #5 (bombardment) — different regimes. Note the ROADMAP's flagged sub-Neptune/Neptunian short-key contradiction (Ice giant (Neptunian) maps to short key sub-neptune, not gas-giant) must be reconciled so the Neptunian preset routes to this writer's low-vigor branch, not falls through to the latitude-band fallback.
acSketch: AC1 (determinism / no-RNG static-source guard, cloned from plates.js AC1): grep the writer source for Math.random/Date.now -> zero hits; same (drivers, macroSeed) twice -> byte-identical carrier.height/grainAngle/grainMag/faultDensity and identical vortex placement array.

AC2 (SHEAR-ZONE PINNING — the architectural-fix gate, the analog of plates' conv>=2x-interior structure bar): every placed great-spot/train vortex center sits in an ANTICYCLONIC shear zone — |corr(vortex latitudes, anticyclonic-shear field)| high; vortices are NOT uniformly distributed in sin(lat) (a chi-square / KS test against the random-latitude null REJECTS uniform). This is what proves placement is history-derived, not a hash sprinkle.

AC3 (Rhines jet-count scaling): njets is monotone in rotation rate and radius; Jovian-driver preset -> ~13-15 jets, Saturnian -> ~11, Neptunian/ice -> ~3 (within tolerance of observed ~20-30 vs ~3); equatorial superrotation jet always present.

AC4 (no-surface field contract): carrier.height carries the signed bright-zone/dark-belt albedo alternation (sign matches anticyclonic/cyclonic classification), grainAngle is azimuthal (zonal), faultDensity = |du/dlat| peaks at jet flanks; bounded |height| < documented GAS_BOUND.
AC5 (great spot scale + aspect): exactly one dominant vortex (storms[0]) with E-W aspect 1.5-2.5 set by ambient meridional shear; angular radius spans ~2 bands (GRS scale).

AC6 (polar vortex variant + M rule): polar M is a closed form from r0/cyclone-deformation-radius; vigor-split chooses lattice (high) / polygonal-jet r(theta)=r0(1+a cos M theta) (mid) / single lobed cap (low); Jovian-class -> M in 5-8 + central, ice -> single cap.
AC7 (regime gate / zero-clobber): on a solid-body regime the writer returns before touching any carrier field — plate/despun/magmatism output byte-identical with and without gasFlow in the dispatch.
AC8 (hot-Jupiter branch): D7 tidalLock set -> njets collapses to 1 equatorial; single bright hotspot vortex at equator offset deterministically EASTWARD of substellar.
AC9 (seed variety): across seeds, jet amplitudes, vortex longitudes, and polar M/orientation differ, but jet COUNT and storm LATITUDES stay driver-locked (history-coherent, not seed-arbitrary).

citations.claim: Zonal jet width/number is set by the Rhines scale L_R ~ sqrt(2U/beta), beta = meridional gradient of the Coriolis parameter; the inverse energy cascade in beta-plane turbulence is arrested at this scale, organizing eddies into alternating zonal jets — this is the codeable basis for deriving jet count from rotation rate and radius.
citations.source: Zonal jets experiments in the gas giants' zonostrophic regime (arXiv 2208.05530); Rhines beta-plane turbulence

citations.claim: Jupiter and Saturn have ~20-30 jets (multiple per hemisphere) while Uranus and Neptune have only ~3 jets (one per hemisphere); simulations reproduce ~20 jets for Jupiter/Saturn and 3 for ice giants, controlled by water abundance, rotation rate, and planetary radius — gives the Jovian/Saturnian/ice-giant jet-count targets and the drivers (D8 rotation, D14 radius, D12/condensables).
citations.source: From gas to ice giants: A unified mechanism for equatorial jets, Science Advances

citations.claim: The Great Red Spot sits at ~22S, confined between a westward jet at ~20S and an eastward jet at ~26S, pinned to a constant latitude by the counter-rotating jets — the anticyclone forms in and is trapped by the jet shear. This is the key fact that storm LATITUDE is a consequence of the jet field, not random.
citations.source: Great Red Spot — confinement by zonal jets (EarthSky / Hubble GRS wind study)

citations.claim: Each giant planet hosts long-lived anticyclones at latitudes corresponding to the first anticyclonic shear zone away from the equator; >90% of Jupiter's visible spots are anticyclonic (white), forming in the strong latitudinal shear between weak zonal winds — directly justifies placing vortices in anticyclonic shear zones rather than random latitudes.
citations.source: Polar and mid-latitude vortices and zonal flows on Jupiter and Saturn, Icarus (ScienceDirect)

citations.claim: Jupiter's polar cyclones form stable 'vortex crystal' polygons: 5 cyclones (pentagon) + 1 central at the south pole, 8 (modified octagon/'double square') + 1 central at the north; ring outer edge ~80-82 deg latitude, ring diameter ~18 deg (~21000 km), individual cyclone diameters 5.5-7 deg latitude; stable over many years — gives the M-count rule and ring radius for the polar-vortex variant.
citations.source: Jupiter's Polar Polygons (British Astronomical Association, Juno results)

citations.claim: Polar polygon stability is explained as a vortex crystal requiring anticyclonic shielding around each cyclone; this packing/shielding constraint is what sets the number of cyclones M in the ring — the deterministic basis for the polar M closed form.
citations.source: Jupiter's Polar Vortex Crystals Explored using the Shallow Water Equations (arXiv 2403.00870); Polygonal patterns of cyclones on Jupiter: Convective forcing and anticyclonic shielding

citations.claim: Saturn's hexagon is a wavenumber-6 Rossby-wave meander of the eastward circumpolar jet near 77-78N (barotropic instability selects azimuthal wavenumber 6); visually the polygon IS a jet streamline r(theta)=r0(1+a cos(N theta)), a closed contour, not a filled shape — gives the polygonal-jet variant's exact closed form.
citations.source: On the dynamical nature of Saturn's North Polar hexagon, Icarus; A Wave Dynamical Interpretation of Saturn's Polar Hexagon

citations.claim: Tidally locked hot Jupiters produce a single broad equatorial superrotating eastward jet (1-7 km/s) maintained by coupled Kelvin-Rossby waves, which shifts the dayside thermal hotspot EASTWARD of the substellar point — the basis for the hot-Jupiter D7 branch (collapse to one equatorial jet + eastward-offset hotspot).
citations.source: Equatorial superrotation on tidally locked exoplanets (arXiv 1103.3101); Atmospheric Circulation of Hot Jupiters (Showman & Polvani)

options: OPTION A (RECOMMENDED) — Jet-lattice -> shear-zone -> vortex writer (gasFlow.js, sub-increment 3b). Derives ALL placement from the jet/shear field: jet lattice (Rhines) -> classify anticyclonic vs cyclonic shear -> place great spot + train in the dominant anticyclonic shear zones, polar vortex as a vortex-crystal/Rossby-meander variant. Writes zonal-flow + cloud-albedo + shear onto the carrier (height repurposed as signed albedo, grainAngle/grainMag as jet vector, faultDensity as shear). PRO: maximal isomorphism with plates.js; truly kills the overlay-divorce (placement is a consequence of the band field); physically honest (matches GRS confinement, Juno polar crystals, Saturn hexagon, hot-Jupiter superrotation); feeds the already-reserved uStorm* carriage. CON: more upfront design than a hash; needs the 3a jet field built/formalized first.

OPTION B — Keep hash placement but CONSTRAIN it to shear zones (minimal). Retain the current rng-driven storm derivation but replace the random latitude (acos(rng.range(-0.7,0.7))) with a SNAP to the nearest anticyclonic shear band computed from the jet profile, and elongate aspect by the local shear. PRO: smallest diff from shipping code; reuses existing PlanetGenerator storm rolls; fast. CON: only half-fixes the divorce (latitude becomes history-derived but the writer is still bolted onto the generator, not a three-free base/ writer; doesn't produce the carrier zonal-flow/albedo fields; polar vortex and hot-Jupiter still ad-hoc; weaker pattern-conformance, harder to test headlessly).

OPTION C — Full pseudo-fluid relaxation field (richest, riskiest). Seed a vorticity field from convective forcing (internal heat as Gaussian convective sources) and run a bounded fixed number of relaxation passes of a discretized vorticity/streamfunction update on the sphere so vortices EMERGE and self-organize into the bands and polar crystals, rather than being placed. PRO: most physically genuine; vortex crystals/polygons could fall out naturally; one mechanism for all variants. CON: skirts the GENERATIVE-NOT-SIMULATIVE rule (a bounded relaxation of a coupled vorticity system is borderline time-stepping and its truncation changes the answer — flagged as the cross-tier fixed-point trap in ROADMAP thin-spot #8); determinism/order-independence hard to prove; far more compute and tuning; high risk for a screensaver-class engine. Not recommended now; possible far-future enrichment.
uncertainties: The exact Rhines-scale constant K for jet count is calibration, not first-principles, for a 4-archetype taste target — I anchored njets to observed counts (~13-15 Jovian, ~11 Saturnian, ~3 ice) but the precise K and vigorFactor must be swept against the F24 bandCount=clamp(round(12*radiusEarth/rotationHours),3,16) the lab already ships so the new writer reproduces (not regresses) the VERIFIED band look. Medium confidence on the form, low on the exact constant.

Which carrier field carries the cloud-albedo signal is a design choice, not forced. I recommend repurposing height (signed) because it is the field the renderer already displaces/reads and keeps the writer-family signature uniform, but an alternative is to add a dedicated carrier.cloudAlbedo field to avoid overloading 'height' semantics on a no-surface body. Worth a quick scope decision; the rest of the design is invariant to it.

The polar M closed form from anticyclonic-shielding/vortex-crystal packing is qualitatively well-grounded (5 S / 8 N at Jupiter, wavenumber-6 at Saturn) but I did not find a clean single published formula M(r0, deformation_radius); the academia.edu source that likely has it returned HTTP 403. I propose M ~ round(2*pi*r_ring / cyclone_spacing) with cyclone diameter ~5.5-7 deg, which reproduces the observed counts, but the exact spacing law is approximate. Medium confidence.

Whether the band/jet field (3a) should be formalized as its own three-free base/ writer or stay in the lab/shader is a sequencing question. F24/F25 already compute u(phi) in the lab shader; 3b ideally reads a base/ jet field for headless testability, which may require lifting some of 3a out of GLSL into base/. Flagging as a scope boundary, not a blocker.

The hot-Jupiter eastward hotspot offset magnitude (~10-60 deg east) varies with wind speed, drag, and even magnetic effects (some ultra-hot Jupiters show WESTWARD offsets via dynamo action). I recommend a deterministic eastward offset as the default branch and note the westward-offset case as an optional extreme-T sub-variant, not v1. Low confidence on the exact offset law; high confidence on 'single equatorial jet + offset hotspot' as the right structure.

Sub-Neptune (hazy) and the Neptunian-via-short-key contradiction (ROADMAP thin-spots #2/#3) are adjacent but out of scope here: this writer covers the gas/ice-giant/hot-Jupiter banded regimes; a near-featureless hazy sub-Neptune may want only a degenerate low-vigor branch (few jets, no discrete spots). Needs Max's call on whether sub-Neptune routes here or to its own thin writer.

verdict.confidence: Medium-high. The core architecture (jet-lattice -> shear-zone -> vortex, isomorphic to plates.js, determinism-clean, generative-not-simulative) is physically sound and well-grounded in the literature, and Option A is the right call. Sound=true is conditional on fixing the equatorial-jet-direction error and the count contradictions below before it goes to a contract — none are fatal to the approach, but AC3/AC4 as written would bake in physically-false behavior.
issues: PHYSICS ERROR (must fix, breaks AC4 and the ice-giant branch): The proposal asserts 'a wide prograde equatorial superrotation jet at lat 0 always present.' This is FALSE for the ice giants, which are explicitly in scope. Uranus and Neptune have RETROGRADE (westward/subrotating) equatorial jets, not prograde superrotation; only Jupiter/Saturn superrotate. Confirmed by Science Advances 'From gas to ice giants' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12513438/ and https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/sciadv.ads8899): 'gas giants exhibit eastward equatorial jets (superrotation) while ice giants show westward equatorial jets (subrotation).' The writer must make the equatorial jet SIGN a deterministic function of regime/vigor (prograde for gas-giant/Saturnian, retrograde for Neptunian/ice, and the modern unified view ties this to convective-envelope DEPTH, a bifurcation), not hardcode 'prograde always.' Since carrier.grainAngle = jet direction and height-sign = anticyclonic/cyclonic classification both flow from u(lat), getting the equatorial sign wrong inverts the visible band luminance and grain at the equator for two of the four archetypes.

PHYSICS / NULL-MODEL ERROR (must fix, contradicts AC2's own stated baseline): The proposal twice states the GRS aspect ratio is 'E-W 1.5-2.5' and 'elongated along latitude' (AC5), and PlanetGenerator.js:629-630 also assumes E-W elongation. The literature is the opposite: the GRS is ~16,350 km E-W by ~24,800 km N-S historically, and its potential-vorticity aspect is ~2:1 with the LONG axis E-W only in the modern shrunken state — but critically the storm is elongated ALONG the zonal (E-W) flow by the jets. The sign of the claim is fine (E-W long axis, stretched by zonal shear) but the proposal's own numbers/phrasing are internally muddled ('aspect 1.5-2.5' vs 'E-W:N-S ~2:1' vs 'elongated along latitude' which reads as N-S). Pin it precisely: vortices are stretched E-W (along the zonal jet) with E-W:N-S aspect ~1.5-2.5, driven by the ambient meridional shear; cite arXiv 1301.6119 (GRS velocity/vorticity) and the universal-vortex-aspect-ratio paper arXiv 1203.1562 for the shear->aspect law rather than a free-floating constant.

SCOPE/ROUTING CONTRADICTION CONFIRMED IN LIVE CODE (must reconcile before contract): I verified PlanetGenerator.js:45 — the live regime keys are gas-giant, hot-jupiter, sub-neptune. There is NO 'Saturnian' or 'Neptunian' short key in the code. The proposal's '4 archetypes have NO relief writer' framing (gas-giant/hot-jupiter/Saturnian/Neptunian) does not map cleanly onto the 3 live keys. The isGasEnvelope regime gate (AC7) cannot be written against regimes that don't exist. Either (a) the Saturnian/Neptunian presets exist only in the planet-lod lab (a different tree), or (b) the archetype-count claim is inflated. This is the same sub-neptune/Neptunian short-key contradiction the proposal flags as ROADMAP thin-spot #2/#3 — it is REAL and unresolved, and it blocks AC7. Resolve the regime taxonomy first; the gate and the vigor-branch selection (gas/Saturnian/ice) both depend on it.

UNVERIFIED ARCHITECTURAL-FIT CLAIM (flag, weakens the 'no new render path' selling point): The proposal repeatedly claims the writer 'feeds the ALREADY-RESERVED uStormPosSize[8]/uStormParams[8]/uStormColor[8]/uStormCount shader carriage' so 'no new uniforms needed.' I grep'd src/ for 'uStorm' across the whole well-dipper tree: ZERO hits. polarStorm DOES exist (PlanetGenerator.js, as claimed). So the polarStorm half of the contract is real but the uStorm[8] carriage is NOT present in src/ — it may live in the planet-lod lab tree or in .glsl assets the grep missed, but as stated the 'reserved carriage exists, zero new render path' claim is unverified and possibly overstated. An engineer should confirm the uStorm uniforms actually exist before relying on 'no new render path,' or the design needs to add them (which is fine, but changes the effort estimate).

DEPENDENCY GAP (flag, real blocker for headless testability): The proposal's whole AC2 (shear-zone pinning) requires reading a base/ jet field u(lat), but there is NO gas/jet writer in src/worldengine/base/ today (confirmed: base/ contains only adaptL0, baseStep, fieldViz, mathutil, plates, sphereField, substrate, tectonic, verify). The proposal acknowledges this (3a must be formalized, F25's u(phi) lives in GLSL) but lists it as a 'soft' / 'scope boundary, not a blocker.' For a HEADLESS-TESTABLE three-free writer (the plates.js discipline the whole program is built on), 3a being GLSL-only is a HARD prerequisite, not soft: AC1/AC2/AC3 cannot run headless if the jet profile only exists in a shader. Promote '3a must be lifted into a base/ writer' to a hard dependency of 3b.

DETERMINISM — minor but worth nailing: The proposal says vortex LATITUDES are deterministically SELECTED (argmax of anticyclonic shear), RNG only sets longitudes/aspect/size. Good — but argmax on a discrete carrier mesh can be order-dependent on ties (two shear zones with near-equal |du/dlat|). To clone the plates.js AC1 byte-identical guarantee, the tie-break must itself be deterministic (e.g. lowest latitude wins, then lowest node index), not 'first seen' in an unspecified iteration order. Specify the tie-break rule in the contract or AC1's byte-identical claim can silently fail across mesh orderings.

GENERATIVE-NOT-SIMULATIVE — Option C correctly rejected, and the recommended Option A's bounded RELAX_PASSES Jacobi smooth is genuinely safe (convex combination over carrier.adj, identical to plates.js lines 268-277, cannot expand bounds, no convergence loop). No time-stepping smell in Option A. One thing to keep honest: the smooth is applied to the height/albedo field only (as in plates.js); do NOT extend it to 'relax the vortex positions' or it would creep toward simulation. Keep placement a pure deterministic selection + RNG-jitter, smoothing only the scalar band field.

HOT-JUPITER BRANCH — physics is right but the proposal already half-flags the caveat; make it explicit in the AC: eastward hotspot offset is the correct DEFAULT (hydrodynamic advection by the superrotating jet), confirmed by Showman & Polvani / arXiv 1103.3101. BUT ultra-hot Jupiters (T_eq >~2000-2400 K) can show ZERO or WESTWARD offset via subcritical dynamo / MHD Lorentz forces (arXiv 2407.12434, Nature Astronomy CoRoT-2b s41550-017-0351-6). The proposal relegates this to 'optional extreme-T sub-variant, not v1' — that's a reasonable scope call, but since D1 (T_eq) is already a driver, AC8 should at minimum NOT assert 'always eastward' unconditionally; gate the eastward default on T_eq below the MHD threshold so a future westward branch isn't a contradiction of a shipped AC.

thinSpots.gap: Venus-like stagnant-lid silicate has no real procedural-history relief writer. The despun/ice-shell writer (#1) EXPLICITLY EXCLUDES Venus (its own increment-1-shell-relief-DESIGN.md, Scope-OUT: "tessera + coronae + global volcanic resurfacing is a mantle-plume/resurfacing primitive with NO ice shell and NO despin-lineament organizing field ... Forcing it through a tidal-stress writer would be physically false AND would pollute the structure test. EXCLUDED"). The volcanic/endogenic-heat writer #4/E7 (magmatism.js) is "assigned" Venus in the ROADMAP coverage map, but its scoped feature set (hotspot/edifice placement + effusive lava-plain flooding + substellar magma-ocean basin) has NO stagnant-lid branch — nothing in it writes tessera fabric, coronae, or a global resurfacing-age field. So Venus, the single most-recognizable non-Earth rocky world, currently falls through to the sin^2(latitude) zonal fallback in tectonic.js (same banded smear as 8 other archetypes). The lab routes its "Venus (sulfuric shroud)" NAMED_BODY through tectonic-terrestrial+volcanic tags, neither of which produces stagnant-lid structure. This is ROADMAP thin-spot #2.
thinSpots.restatement: Build a dedicated DETERMINISTIC, GENERATIVE-NOT-SIMULATIVE relief writer for the stagnant-lid silicate regime (Venus-class: a single immobile lithospheric plate punctured by mantle plumes, no plate-boundary belts, no ice shell, no despin lineaments). It must place the determined END-STATE of a stagnant-lid history in ONE pass plus a bounded fixed number of Jacobi relaxation passes, following the proven plates.js template (seeded centroids/field -> classify -> REPLACE carrier.height -> bounded relax -> regime gate), three-free in src/worldengine/base, every random draw via alea(seedString) keyed off the integer macroSeed (NEVER Math.random/Date.now). The three signature Venus structures it must synthesize: (1) tessera fabric — old, high, intensely double-deformed crustal-plateau terrain (orthogonal ribbon+fold lineaments, ~7-8% of surface, 1-5 km high); (2) coronae — circular plume-driven volcano-tectonic features (60-2600 km, raised rim + concentric/radial fracture annulus + interior depression or dome, ~the BAT-region clustering along rifts); (3) a global volcanic resurfacing-AGE field — most of the surface is one young (~300-700 Myr) basaltic regional-plains datum, recording near-synchronous catastrophic/episodic resurfacing, with younger lobate flows near plume centers. It REPLACES carrier.height for stagnant-lid bodies only and never touches the plate or shell paths.
thinSpots.recommendedApproach:
Build a new sibling writer `writeStagnantLidReliefSphere(carrier, drivers={}, { macroSeed=0, tune=null })` in a NEW file `src/worldengine/base/stagnantLid.js`, modeled byte-for-byte on the plates.js / shellRelief.js discipline (copy dot/cross/norm/randDir/falloffAng + the meanEdgeAngle resolution-key verbatim; disjoint `'stag:'` alea namespace). Mechanism, in plates.js phase order:

STEP 0 — RESOLUTION KEY: meanEdgeAngle = mean acos(dot(verts[i],verts[nb])) over adj edges (verbatim plates.js:126-131). All widths in GEODESIC RADIANS -> BFS hops, resolution-independent.

STEP 1 — SEED THE PLUME / TESSERA / RESURFACING FIELDS (analog of plates seeding centroids):
 - K_corona plume centers via `'stag:plumes:'+seed` (K = CORONA_MIN + floor(rng()*CORONA_SPAN), default [8,16] ~ matching the few-hundred catalogued large coronae scaled down). Each gets: randDir centroid; a radius drawn in GEODESIC radians from CORONA_R_MIN..MAX (so size varies 60-2600 km analog); an `active` flag (rng()<CORONA_ACTIVE_FRAC, default ~0.35 — only ~20-35% show rim+trench plume-active morphology); a polarity. Cite: 740 catalogued coronae 60-2600 km (Nature Geoscience 2020); ~133 large coronae, ~active outer-rise+trench vs inactive rim+inner-depression (Springer Nature hotspot-Venus 2020).
 - M_tessera plateau seeds via `'stag:tessera:'+seed` (M = TESSERA_MIN + floor(rng()*TESSERA_SPAN), default [2,5] — few crustal plateaus, e.g. Ishtar/Aphrodite), each a centroid + geodesic radius; tessera total area is held to ~TESSERA_AREA_FRAC (default 0.08) of the sphere (8% of surface). Cite: tessera ~7.3% of surface, exposed within crustal plateaus, 1-5 km high (Wikipedia Tessera; Britannica Aphrodite/Ishtar).
 - A "RIFT NETWORK" via a low-freq domain-warped great-circle band field `'stag:rift:'+seed`: 2-4 seeded great-circle-ish chasmata that PREFERENTIALLY connect plume centers (BAT-region Parga/Hecate/Devana chasmata link Beta-Atla-Themis). Implement as: for each rift, two endpoint plume centers, the rift node-membership = nodes within RIFT_HALF_WIDTH geodesic of the minor-arc between them, warped by simplex. Cite: corona-type features strongly associate with rifts; BAT triple-junction (Airey 2017 JGR; LPI BAT 2010).
 - noise3D fields: `'stag:warp:'` (warp all centers/arcs so nothing is a clean great circle), `'stag:fabric:'` (tessera ribbon+fold steered-ridged texture), `'stag:plains:'` (sub-grid regional-plains texture).

STEP 2 — CLASSIFY each node into a STAGNANT-LID UNIT (analog of plates boundary classification). For node i compute geodesic distances to nearest plume center (d_cor), nearest tessera seed (d_tes), nearest rift (d_rift) via multi-source BFS (O(N) queue drain, NOT time-stepping). Unit precedence (oldest-to-youngest stratigraphy, highest precedence wins):
   UNIT_TESSERA  if d_tes < tessera radius AND cumulative tessera area budget not exceeded (deterministic: sort candidates by d_tes, fill until TESSERA_AREA_FRAC reached);
   UNIT_CORONA_ANNULUS if d_cor within [r*RIM_INNER, r*RIM_OUTER] of a plume (the fractured rim);
   UNIT_CORONA_INTERIOR if d_cor < r*RIM_INNER (central depression/dome);
   UNIT_RIFT if d_rift < RIFT_HALF_WIDTH;
   else UNIT_PLAINS (the ~70-80% regional volcanic plains datum).
   Store unit[i] (Uint8) — the geometric, U-independent label the structure test rebuilds proximity from (arm's-length, like plates boundaryClass).

STEP 3 — WRITE THE END-STATE HEIGHT FIELD U (REPLACE) per unit:
   PLAINS: U = PLAINS_BASE + small DETAIL (the flat young basaltic datum). Wrinkle-ridge micro-relief = low-amp steered ridged noise (gentle compression).
   TESSERA: U = TESSERA_BASE (high, +1-5 km analog) + TESSERA_FABRIC_AMP * orthogonalRidged(d, theta_fabric) — TWO superimposed steered-ridged-noise sets at ~orthogonal strikes (ribbons ⟂ folds), the double-deformation signature. theta_fabric written to carrier.grainAngle.
   CORONA: analytic radial cross-section as a function of (d_cor / r): a raised RIM bump (Gaussian/ smoothstep ring at d_cor~r), an interior depression (active: deep trench just outside rim + outer rise; inactive: inner depression) selected by the `active` flag, central small dome if active. Concentric+radial fracture amplitude added in the annulus (faultDensity). Cite cross-section: active = outer rise + deep trench; inactive = outer rim + inner depression (Springer Nature 2020).
   RIFT: linear graben trough along the arc + flanking shoulders (extensional chasmata).

STEP 4 — RESURFACING-AGE FIELD (the field with NO Earth-analog in plates — the Venus-specific extra): write a per-node `resurfaceAge[i]` in [0,1] (0=youngest). Mechanism: global synchronous young base age AGE_BASE (catastrophic/episodic resurfacing ~300-700 Myr -> near-uniform young), MINUS youthening near active plume centers/rifts (lobate flows postdate regional plains), PLUS aging on tessera (oldest stratigraphic unit, pre-resurfacing relict). resurfaceAge = clamp01(AGE_BASE - YOUTH_GAIN*falloff(d_cor_active) - YOUTH_GAIN*falloff(d_rift) + OLD_GAIN*isTessera). This is the field that ENCODES the history (which downstream palette/E12 + the player reads as "uniformly young plains with old tessera islands"). Cite: 84% craters pristine, only 2.5% embayed -> near-synchronous young surface; lobate plains + rift youngest (Strom 1994 JGR; Hunter Heidenreich stratigraphy notes).

STEP 5 — ASSEMBLE + BOUNDED RELAX + GATE: carrier.height.set(U) (REPLACE, sole low/mid source); fixed RELAX_PASSES (default 4) Jacobi smooth (verbatim plates h*0.5+mean*0.5 double-buffered convex combination — cannot expand bound); assert |U| < STAG_BOUND. carrier.faultDensity[i] = clamp01(annulus/tessera-fabric/rift stress proxy) (parity with plates faultDensity=|boundaryStress|). carrier.grainAngle[i] = tessera fabric strike (in tessera) / radial-or-concentric fracture strike (in annulus) / rift strike — reusing the grain channel exactly as writeGrainSphere does.

ALL TUNABLES LOCKED in a frozen STAG_DEFAULTS, override-able ONLY by the headless structure test via `tune`, never by route()/lab — identical discipline to plates DEFAULTS.
thinSpots.fieldsWritten:
There IS a surface height to REPLACE (Venus is a solid silicate body), so this writer REPLACES carrier.height exactly like plates.js. Fields written:
 - carrier.height[i] = U[i] via carrier.height.set(U) — REPLACE (=, never +=), the SOLE low/mid-frequency source for stagnant-lid bodies. (high tessera plateaus + corona rims/depressions + rift grabens on a flat young-plains datum.)
 - carrier.grainAngle[i] = unit-dependent lineament strike: tessera ribbon/fold fabric angle in tessera, concentric/radial fracture angle in corona annuli, rift strike in chasmata, ~0/low in plains. (Reuses the carrier grain channel exactly as writeGrainSphere/shellRelief do.)
 - carrier.faultDensity[i] = clamp01 of the local tectonic-activity proxy (tessera double-deformation intensity, corona annulus fracture density, rift extension) — direct parity with plates writing faultDensity=|boundaryStress| and shell writing faultDensity=clamp01(|sigma1|).
 - NEW diagnostic field unique to this regime, returned in the diag object AND optionally written if a carrier channel is added: resurfaceAge[i] in [0,1] (0=youngest). This is the Venus-specific history field that has no Earth/plate analog — it records the global resurfacing-age pattern (uniformly young plains, old tessera relicts, youngest near active plumes/rifts). Recommend returning it in the diagnostics object this increment (peer of plateDiag/shellDiag) and consuming it in the later E12 palette pass, rather than adding a carrier channel now (sphereField.js has no age channel; keep the carrier contract stable per the no-new-channel discipline plates/shell followed).
 Diagnostics returned (peer of plateDiag): { U, regime:'stagnant-lid', unit:Uint8Array, coronaId:Int32Array, coronaActive:Uint8Array, tesseraMask:Uint8Array, riftMask:Uint8Array, resurfaceAge:Float32Array, thetaFabric:Float32Array, plumeCenters:[[x,y,z]], coronaCount:int, tesseraAreaFrac:number, meanEdgeAngle, relaxPasses }.
thinSpots.deterministicMechanism: Identical determinism contract to plates.js/shellRelief.js: every entropy source is alea(seedString) keyed off seed=(macroSeed|0); NO Math.random / NO Date.now anywhere incl. helpers. Disjoint 'stag:' alea namespace (stag:plumes / stag:tessera / stag:rift / stag:warp / stag:fabric / stag:plains) so it never shares a stream with plates ('plates:'), shell ('shell:'), or tectonic ('e6:'). Same (drivers, macroSeed) => byte-identical U/grainAngle/faultDensity/unit/coronaId/resurfaceAge (enforced by an AC1 no-RNG static-source grep + double-run Float32Array byte-equality, cloned from the plate/shell AC1). GENERATIVE-NOT-SIMULATIVE: the determined end-state is placed in ONE pass; the only iteration is (a) the O(N) multi-source BFS distance transform (each node enqueued exactly once — a graph distance transform, NOT a time loop) and (b) the bounded fixed RELAX_PASSES Jacobi smooth (a convex combination that cannot expand the bound). NO per-Myr time-stepping, NO while-loop on a convergence threshold. The "resurfacing-age" field is placed as a closed-form end-state (global young datum minus plume/rift youthening plus tessera aging), NOT simulated by stepping crater accumulation. Deterministic tie-breaks: tessera area budget filled by sorting candidates by ascending geodesic distance and integer index (strict < / strict > like the plates Voronoi tie-break) so the 8% area cap is reproducible; corona-unit precedence resolved by a fixed precedence order (tessera > corona-interior > corona-annulus > rift > plains), not float-fragile comparisons. Crest/threshold rules (tessera fabric crests, corona annulus bands) are THRESHOLD-based on geodesic distance (order-independent, resolution-independent), not relative local-maxima — matching the shell DESIGN MUST-FIX #1(e).
thinSpots.architecturalFit: Fits the proven family pattern WITHOUT a bag-of-overlays, on five points: (1) It IS the plates.js template re-keyed for a single-plate body: instead of plate centroids -> Voronoi -> boundary stress, it is plume/tessera/rift centroids -> distance-classified units -> end-state relief, with the SAME phase order (seed -> classify -> REPLACE height -> bounded relax -> faultDensity parity). (2) CLASSIFY — compute a single scalar `hazeOpacity` in [0,1] from drivers via a CLOSED FORM: hazeOpacity = hazeTempBell(T_eq) * volatileGate, where hazeTempBell is a parabola/Gaussian peaking in the empirically-observed 500-800 K window (Crossfield & Kreidberg 2017 parabolic trend; hydrocarbon hazes dominate at T_eq<=850-950 K, soot-factory paper). Sub-class flag (haze regime) fires when (composition=='h2-he' && radiusEarth<6 && massEarth<10 && hazeOpacity>THRESH) — IDENTICAL gate to the shader's existing cloudRegime-2 (lab:3345), now computed once in the writer. citations.claim: GJ 1214 b's near-IR transmission spectrum is flat/featureless, implying high-altitude aerosols (photochemical haze and/or condensate clouds) that prevent probing the atmosphere below; very high metallicity (>=1000x solar) and high haze production are needed to match it.

citations.claim: Muted/flat sub-Neptune spectra occur preferentially over a constrained equilibrium-temperature range ~500-800 K, following a tentative parabolic spectral trend with T_eq (Crossfield & Kreidberg 2017) — the basis for the hazeTempBell closed form.
