issues: VERDICT: Sound, with calibration/scoping caveats. The core architectural call is correct and well-grounded. (1) PHYSICALLY-FALSE-PRIMITIVE: the proposal correctly refuses to write carrier.height — a sub-Neptune is a rocky/icy core under a thick H/He envelope with no observable solid surface (radius valley 1.5-2 R-Earth; sub-Neptunes 2-4 R-Earth with primordial H/He), so there is genuinely no relief to REPLACE. Routing it to E5 (atmosphere/optics) instead of a relief writer is the physically honest move. CONFIRMED vs Small_planet_radius_gap (Wikipedia) and GJ 1214 b JWST work. PASS on test (3).

BAG-OF-OVERLAYS (test 4): PASS. The proposal makes haze a WRITTEN, driver-derived field (the determined photochemical end-state of the envelope given T_eq + composition), folded into the SAME gas-giant band writer as a muted-amplitude branch via a MULTIPLY (bandField *= (1 - hazeMute*hazeOpacity)), not a fifth toggled shader overlay on a historyless substrate. It also explicitly rejects Option C (shader-only) for exactly this reason and proposes making the writer the single source of truth the shader's cloudRegime-2 path currently hardcodes — i.e. it REMOVES a worldengine/shader divergence rather than adding one. Aligned with ROADMAP north star (line 11) and the ROADMAP's own thin-spot-3 (a)-vs-(b) framing (lines 87-89).

DETERMINISM (test 2): PASS. hazeOpacity is a pure closed form of drivers (no RNG); alea('e5:...:'+macroSeed) disjoint namespace matches the plates.js discipline (header lines 31-33) and the existing 'shell:'/'e6:'/'plates:' namespace convention noted in ROADMAP line 122; nBands is a deterministic function of rotationHours; the only iteration is a fixed RELAX_PASSES Jacobi smooth (convex combination, cannot expand bounds) — no time-stepping, no while-on-threshold. Generative-not-simulative single-pass + bounded relax holds. The AC1 no-RNG static-source guard precedent exists (plates.js:33, tectonic.js:79, baseStep.js:3) and is correctly cloned.

HARD DEPENDENCY / BIGGEST RISK (proposal's uncertainty #1) — VERIFIED REAL AND UNDERSTATED. I confirmed in src/worldengine/base/sphereField.js (makeSphereField, lines 11-21) that the carrier has NO band/atmosphere/haze/wind/jet channel — only height/grainAngle/grainMag/regime/faultDensity/flowAccum/baseLevel/standing/maturity. climate-e5.js does NOT exist. Moreover the ROADMAP #3 claims E5 'drops onto pre-built seams (precipWeight, baseLevel)' but grep shows precipWeight does NOT exist in base/ either (only baseLevel). So the entire 'WRITE CARRIER FIELDS' half of Option A is blocked until E5 (a) defines a band/haze channel on the carrier AND (b) is built at all. The proposal flags this but frames it as a soft 'likely needs'; it is a hard precondition. Recommendation stands BUT must be explicitly scoped as a sub-branch of E5/#3, never ahead of it (proposal says this — good).

PHYSICS OVER-CLAIM TO FLAG (single-jet collapse): the 'collapse toward a single superrotating equatorial jet confined to +/-20deg as hazeOpacity rises' is real and well-cited (Steinrueck/adc99a: 'transitions to a single superrotating equatorial jet if haze opacity is sufficiently high... confined to +/-20deg of latitude'), BUT that GCM study models ONLY TIDALLY-LOCKED GJ 1214 b-like planets (rotation = orbital period 1.58 d). The lab's Sub-Neptune preset is tidalState.locked:false. Applying the locked-regime single-jet/day-night-contrast result to a non-locked sub-Neptune is an extrapolation beyond the cited source. The band-MUTING (contrast collapse) is on firmer ground (parabolic muted-spectrum trend is rotation-agnostic); the JET-COLLAPSE-to-single-equatorial-jet specifically should be softened or gated on tidal lock, or labeled as artistic-license, not presented as established for the unlocked case.

PHYSICS — hazeTempBell shape: the 500-800 K muted-window and Teq<=950 K hydrocarbon-haze / >950 K silicate bifurcation are CONFIRMED (multiple sources incl. soot-factory ApJL and HD 86226 c A&A). But the literature is more specific than the proposal's symmetric Gaussian: large features are seen BELOW ~400 K and ABOVE ~700 K with muting peaking 500-800 K. A Gaussian centered 650 K, width 180 K still yields ~0.46 opacity at 400 K and ~0.46 at 900 K — it does not fall off fast enough at the window edges to match 'clear below 400 K / clear above 700 K.' For the two TARGET presets it doesn't matter (T_eq 55 K -> ~0 below the 350 K hard cutoff; 550 K -> ~0.74 >0.7 threshold, both ACs pass), but if E5 ever sweeps intermediate-T h2-he bodies the bell will over-haze the 400 K and 900 K wings. Proposal flags this as tunable — acceptable, but tighten the width or use an asymmetric/narrower window.

DRIVER-PLUMBING ERROR: hazeOpacity = hazeTempBell(T_eq) * volatileGate is partly vestigial. I checked all four h2-he giants (Jovian/Saturnian/Neptunian/Sub-Neptune) carry IDENTICAL volatileFraction:0.04. So volatileGate is a no-op across exactly the presets it must discriminate and contributes nothing to separating Neptunian from Sub-Neptune — that separation comes entirely from hazeTempBell(T_eq) plus the radius<6 && mass<10 gate. Not fatal (the gate is in fact doubly-robust: Neptunian fails on BOTH mass 17.1>10 AND hazeOpacity~0 at 55 K; Sub-Neptune passes on radius 2.7<6, mass 8.2<10, opacity~0.74), but the proposal overstates volatileGate's role. Either diversify the driver or drop the factor.

NUMERIC NITS (verify before coding, per proposal's own uncertainty #5): (a) the lab band-count clamp FLOOR is 3, not 2 — code is Math.max(3, ...) at lab:3092-3093 (12*R/rotH clamped 3..16); the proposal's restated 'clamp(round(k/rotationHours), 2, 16)' has the wrong floor. The roadmap text rhetorically lumps it into increment #1's despun/ice-shell writer (to claim "~5-6 of 11"), but #1's own DESIGN doc EXPLICITLY excludes it, and the next time it could appear is the XL increment #8 (the most-cuttable, most-back-loaded slot, bundled with carbon/crystal/technogenic + 6 Tier-5 overlays). thinSpots.restatement: Build a deterministic worldengine "shatter-and-reaccrete" relief writer (proposed src/worldengine/base/shatter.js, export writeShatterReliefSphere) that is a fourth sibling of the existing earthlike-plate / shell-relief dispatch family. It must follow the proven plates.js discipline exactly: three-free (alea + simplex + mathutil only, never imports three); GENERATIVE-NOT-SIMULATIVE (place the determined END-STATE of one disruption-reassembly event in ONE pass, NOT time-step the fragmentation); fully deterministic (every draw via alea(seedString) keyed off integer macroSeed, in a disjoint 'shatter:' namespace, zero Math.random/Date.now); seeded fragment partition -> classify boundaries -> REPLACE carrier.height -> a fixed bounded number of Jacobi relax passes -> gated behind a regime check so it never touches the validated plate path or the shell path. It is also the history-data PRODUCER that the already-spec'd shader-side F45 'shatterCombiner' (Voronoi block field) should read, instead of the shader re-inventing blocks from pure noise divorced from history.
thinSpots.recommendedApproach:
RECOMMENDED = Option B: "reaccreted-rubble Voronoi block writer with per-block rigid SE(3)-style tilt + grabenized boundaries." This is the most faithful to BOTH the catastrophic-disruption science and the proven writer pattern, and it is the smallest writer that produces the three load-bearing reads (discrete rigid tilted blocks / sharp carved-down fault seams / two scales). Concrete codeable pipeline, mirroring plates.js step-for-step:

(0) GATE / REGIME (mirrors plates.js route boundary): dispatch fires only when route() resolves the body to regime 'exotic-shattered' (lab short key 'shatter'/'shattered' and canonical 'exotic-shattered'). Checked AFTER isEarthlikePlatePath returns false AND after shellRegimeOf returns null, so it provably never clobbers the plate path or the shell path (clone the AC7 no-clobber test). It is its OWN regime tag, NOT a member of SHELL_EXCLUDE/shell regimes.

(1) SEED FRAGMENT CENTROIDS (mirrors plates.js seed-centroids): draw FRAG_COUNT in [FRAG_MIN=18, FRAG_MIN+FRAG_SPAN] (span 30 => ~18-48 reaccreted mega-fragments; far more than plates' 7-13, because a rubble pile has many blocks) via rngCount=alea('shatter:count:'+seed); place each centroid with randDir(alea('shatter:centroid:'+seed)) (the exact z=2u-1 / azimuth-2*pi*v helper from plates.js). Two-scale: ALSO draw a sub-fracture frequency multiplier SUB_FREQ (~3.5) — block interiors get a second-octave fine fracture lattice so the disc reads "violently reassembled," not "uniform paving stones."

(2) VORONOI PARTITION with DOMAIN-WARPED boundaries (mirrors plates.js spherical-Voronoi): fragId[i] = argmax over centroids of dot(warpedDir(verts[i]), centroid), where warpedDir applies the SAME low-freq 3D-simplex domain warp plates.js uses (createNoise3D(alea('shatter:warp:'+seed)), WARP_FREQ~1.5, WARP_AMP~0.22) so block seams are irregular, not great-circle/soap-bubble-regular (matches F45 UAT "irregular crack lines"). This is the "shattered into fragments" half.

(3) PER-FRAGMENT RIGID ATTITUDE = the reaccretion physics (this is the writer's distinctive primitive, replacing plates.js Euler-pole motion). Each reaccreted fragment lands at a RANDOM rigid orientation — gravitationally-bound reassembly does NOT restore the original smooth figure; blocks are mutually mis-tilted with offset base elevations. For each fragment p draw, from alea('shatter:attitude:'+seed):
   - blockBase[p] = (rngAtt()*2-1) * BLOCK_OFFSET (BLOCK_OFFSET~0.5): the radial step of that block (some sit proud, some sunken — the "mismatched provinces" read).
   - tiltAxis[p] = a random unit vector in the LOCAL tangent plane at the centroid (project a randDir onto the tangent frame via carrier.tangentFrameAt-style east/north), and tiltMag[p] = rngAtt() * MAX_TILT (MAX_TILT~0.18 rad). The block's surface is a PLANE tilted by (tiltAxis,tiltMag): for node i in fragment p, blockTilt = tiltMag[p] * dot(localOffset(i,centroid_p), tiltAxisTangent[p]), where localOffset is the geodesic tangent displacement of node i from its fragment centroid. CONSTANT per-block gradient => each block's interior is a flat/uniformly-tilted plate (the F45 "rigid plate, lands in its own posterize band" requirement; this is exactly the chaosCombiner "constant tilt gradient" promoted to global scale).
   - rawHeight[i] = blockBase[fragId[i]] + blockTilt(i).

(4) CLASSIFY BOUNDARIES + WRITE FAULT RELIEF (mirrors plates.js classify-by-relative-motion, but the discriminant is MISMATCH not stress): for every node i with a cross-fragment neighbor j (fragId[j] != fragId[i]), mark isBoundary[i]=1 and compute mismatch[i] = the largest |rawHeight[i] - rawHeight[j]| across its cross-fragment edges (the scarp throw). Two boundary effects, both keyed off mismatch:
   - a GRABEN CARVE-DOWN at the seam: subtract SEAM_DEPTH * exp(-geodesicDist/SEAM_BELT) so seams read as carved-DOWN crevasses with cliff walls (reuse the angular falloffAng(dist,belt) form from plates.js; SEAM_BELT~0.02 rad — narrow, sharp, resolution-independent via meanEdgeAngle just like plates.js BELT_RADIANS). This is the Verona-Rupes / chasma read and the F45 "carved-DOWN crevasse" UAT item.
   - record the seam as a fault in carrier.faultDensity (see fieldsWritten).

(5) BOUNDED RELAX — but ASYMMETRIC to preserve sharp seams (the one deliberate divergence from plates.js, justified below): run RELAX_PASSES=2 (fewer than plates' 4) of the SAME convex Jacobi smooth (h*0.5 + mean(self+neighbors)*0.5, double-buffered, cannot expand the bound) ONLY on non-boundary nodes — boundary nodes are pinned. Smooths within-block micro-noise without rounding off the block edges that ARE the signal. (If a strictly-identical-to-plates relax is preferred for pattern purity, run the unmasked smooth at RELAX_PASSES=1; either is bounded and deterministic.)

(6) REPLACE: carrier.height.set(rawHeight_after_seams_and_relax) — '=' REPLACE, the sole low/mid-frequency source for this body (exactly as plates.js writes U with REPLACE, never +=, to avoid re-introducing the latitude-band fallback).

NAMED CONSTANTS (LOCKED, in a frozen DEFAULTS object exactly like plates.js): FRAG_MIN=18, FRAG_SPAN=30, WARP_FREQ=1.5, WARP_AMP=0.22, BLOCK_OFFSET=0.5, MAX_TILT=0.18, SEAM_DEPTH=0.6, SEAM_BELT=0.02, SUB_FREQ=3.5, SUB_AMP=0.12, RELAX_PASSES=2, H_BOUND=4.

issues: FALSE CODEBASE CLAIM — maturity/baseLevel/standing are ALREADY WRITTEN with conflicting semantics (the most serious issue). The proposal's uncertainty #3 states 'grep shows only verify.js touches it [maturity] today, so likely safe.' That is WRONG. relief-e9-hydrology.js:149 already writes substrate.maturity[i] = min(1, maturity + maturity*0.5) with the semantics of EROSION-AGE/terrain maturity (line 116: maturity = clamp(0.4 + 0.6*age)), and relief-e9-hydrology.js:147-148 already writes substrate.standing (lake/sea mask) and substrate.baseLevel (water-surface elevation: sea -> seaLevel, lake -> filled level). planet-lod-uniforms.js, planet-lod-height.glsl.js, and planet-archetypes.js also CONSUME a 'maturity/coverage' uniform. So carrier.maturity is NOT a free channel — the proposal's plan to REPURPOSE it as 'deposition/accommodation potential' collides head-on with (a) E9's erosion-age meaning AND (b) the spine's own E8b 'regolith-maturity' (space-weathering nanophase-iron albedo, spine line 86). That is THREE incompatible meanings for one channel. Same problem for baseLevel: proposal calls it 'allocated-but-unwritten, the natural home for a shelf/relief datum' but E9 already defines it as the hydrological water-surface base-level. Overloading either silently corrupts the E9 hydrology editor the proposal itself lists as a #7 consumer. FIX: the proposal must either add NEW carrier channels (carrier.accommodation, carrier.sediment) or reconcile with E9's existing baseLevel/maturity semantics — not assume they are empty.

NONEXISTENT WRITER REFERENCED AS A DEPENDENCY — 'shellRelief' (with thetaTraj / cellId / w0 / t_hat) is cited ~15 times as a concrete source the figure/orientation/province sub-fields READ FROM, but shellRelief.js does NOT exist in the codebase. grep for shellRelief / thetaTraj returns ZERO hits in src. The roadmap names shellRelief.js as increment #1, which is DESIGNED-but-NOT-BUILT ('none yet built beyond #1's build-ready design', ROADMAP.md:37). So 5.5's stated hard dependency ('depends on at least TWO relief regimes existing — shell + plates') is unmet today; ONLY plates.js is shipped. This is consistent with 5.5 landing after #1, but the proposal should state plainly that figure's 'reuse shellRelief's w0/t_hat' and province's 'shellRelief cellId' are dependencies on UNBUILT code, not on existing fields. The actual current despun/shell-adjacent writer is relief-e6-tectonic.js / tectonic.js writeGrainSphere, whose grain is a pure function of LATITUDE (tectonic.js:51-62) and which computes NO spin axis w0 or cellId — so the figure descriptor cannot 'reuse' a paleo-spin vector that no shipped writer produces. Figure must originate w0 itself (from drivers), not 'reuse' it.

REGIME CHANNEL CANNOT HOLD THE PROPOSED PROVINCE/REGIME RICHNESS AS-IS — carrier.regime is a Uint8 HARD-CONSTRAINED by verify.js:39 to exactly {0,1,2} = {NORMAL, STRIKESLIP, THRUST} (substrate.js:4). The proposal's (d) says it will 'GUARANTEE carrier.regime populated per Anderson THRUST/STRIKESLIP/NORMAL' which is fine, BUT the bounded-ness gate in verify.js will FAIL if any path leaves regime at a value outside {0,1,2}. The curvature-fallback derivation ('regime from sign of mean-curvature') must map to exactly those three integers or the existing verify gate breaks. Minor but must be pinned in the AC, since AC1 claims 'all fields finite + bounded' — the existing bounded gate is stricter than the proposal acknowledges.

CYCLE-1 'MASS-CONSERVING' CLAIM IS PHYSICALLY OVERSTATED AS SCOPED — the sediment field is sound as a host (source-to-sink box model verified: erosion zone -> transfer -> sink with conserved budget, Journal of Geology / Sediment Routing Systems). BUT the proposal makes carrier.maturity = smoothstep(baseLevel - height), i.e. ACCOMMODATION (how far below base a node sits), and then claims #7 erosion 'deposits removed mass into high-maturity sinks ... leaving the total height-integral conserved.' Accommodation-potential is NOT the same as a mass budget: smoothstep saturates, so a deep basin and a very deep basin can have equal maturity=1 yet wildly different capacity. Mass conservation requires the deposit step to track ACTUAL volume routed vs ACTUAL remaining capacity (a true budget), which a saturating [0,1] potential cannot represent. This is exactly the conflation roadmap thin-spot #8 warns about ('bounded relaxation passes' vs 'fixed-point cycle resolution'). The 5.5 pass can legitimately provide the SINK-RANKING field, but should NOT claim it makes CYCLE-1 mass-conserving — that requires #6 to own a real volumetric budget.
